correctness.rationale: Exact normalized wheel metric yields polytope |x_i|≤r and |x_i-x_{i+1}|≤1. Each vertex iff the spanning tight-edge graph is connected by graph-incidence rank m+1-c; a tight path from hub forces every coordinate to ±r+j, which under 1/2<r<1 gives precisely four values. An a must touch A and b must touch B, with A/B opposite adjacency forbidden, and conversely these local conditions make the whole tight graph hub-connected. The 14 pair-state transfer gives the number for every m≥4, and an integer Newton-identity computation checks det(zI-T)=z^9(z²-z+1)(z³-z²-3z-2). The general asymptotic follows from cubic roots. Standalone verifier independently enumerates every rational active basis for m=3,4,5 at r=3/4; endpoints are treated separately. No finite computation is mistaken for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Facet count of the real Lipschitz-free unit ball is a natural isometry-invariant polyhedral norm property and counts the extreme norming Lipschitz potentials. The wheel is a classical published graph family. Varying the hub-to-rim distance is a motivated one-parameter metric deformation with a novel constant combinatorial phase, a nontrivial 14-state cyclic-word characterization and a different exact exponential growth rate; at m=4 there is an actual 16→38→26 endpoint pattern. Endpoint values and general tight-rank criteria are not claimed as novel. This has a clear use for geometry/complexity of graph transportation norms.
